@arv/structs

The TC39 structs proposal for JavaScript today: structs, shared structs, SharedArray, Atomics.Mutex and Atomics.Condition, with a compiler for their syntax.

@arv/structs is an implementation of the TC39 structs proposal (Stage 2, the December 2024 draft) for JavaScript today: structs, shared structs, Shared Arrays, Atomics.Mutex and Atomics.Condition. It has a runtime that follows the spec's algorithms, and a compiler for the proposal's syntax. In TypeScript, the compiler also uses the types to make shared struct field access direct. 

shared struct Counter {
  count = 0;
  lock = new Atomics.Mutex();
}

const counter = new Counter();
worker.postMessage(counter); // the same object in the worker, not a copy

// in any agent:
{
  using _ = Atomics.Mutex.lock(counter.lock);
  counter.count++;
}

You can write programs and run them in your browser, with the compiled JavaScript side by side, in the playground.

Status: experimental

This is the tc39-proposal branch of arv/threads. It replaces the threads library on main with something much smaller that stays as close to the spec as JavaScript allows. See Differences from the Spec.

What's in It

Spec Here
§1 struct declarations The compiler lowers them to classes that call the runtime
§2 shared struct declarations Proxies over one growable SharedArrayBuffer, the heap
§2.3 Atomics on struct fields load, store, exchange and compareExchange take a struct
§2.4 Reflect.canBeShared Installed on Reflect
§3 SharedArray A global: a Shared Struct with indexed fields and a fixed length
§4 Atomics.Mutex, UnlockToken Futex-style locks on heap words; tokens work with using
§4 Atomics.Condition wait, waitFor (with a timeout and a predicate), notify

Importing @arv/structs installs the globals. The compiler's output imports @arv/structs/runtime, which does it too.
